newsitem.title: NORWAY: FORECAST - Kvaerner Q1 pretax seen at NOK 149 mln.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Kvaerner Q1 pretax seen at NOK 149 mln.

text.p: Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner ASA is expected to post first-quarter profits before tax at 149 million crowns, according to a Reuter poll of nine Norwegian and international analysts.
There was no comparative year-ago figure, which will be calculated on a pro forma basis following Kvaerner's takeover of British conglomerate Trafalgar House Plc in April, 1996.
Five of the analysts recommended to buy the share, two said hold, one said sell and one declined to give a recommendation.
The analysts said developments in the loss-making pulp division would be one of the most interesting figures, as well as whether the oil and gas business fell in the red or the black.
Many of the analysts said they expected pulping to continue the negative performance seen in the second half of 1996.
"The loss-making contracts will not be off the books until the second half of this year," commented one analyst.
But many analysts said the London-based group had potential to double its share price, although some said it was a long way off.

"They don't deserve to be priced at a premium at the moment because judging by their track record Kvaerner should be at a discount. But I don't have any problem saying that Kvaerner has the potential to double share price in the future," said another analyst.
At 1108 GMT Kvaerner's A and B stock stood one crown up at 364 crowns and 334 crowns respectively.
